tasks.title: Record the write-scope and static-check baseline before any change
tasks.detail:
Goal: Freeze the starting state of a dirty tree so every later check is a DIFFERENCE against a recorded snapshot instead of an absolute status list — the tree already carries another feature's modifications and untracked files, and it keeps changing while this plan runs (it gained components/JsonTree.{tsx,test.mjs} between audit rounds).
Files: create ONLY `.ppm/system-prompt-markdown-panel/baseline.txt`. Do not modify, stage, stash or clean anything: no `git add`, no `git checkout`, no `git clean`, no formatter, no `next build`. Another feature is in flight; its files must stay exactly as they are.
Contract: the file is plain text with FIVE sections in this order, each under a `## ` heading and each holding raw command output: `## status` (full `git status --porcelain=v1`), `## diffstat` (`git diff --stat`), `## perfile` (one line `added=<added-line count> <path>` for every path in `git diff --name-only`, from `git diff --numstat` column 1 — the added-lines column, not `git diff | wc -l`, which also counts context and headers), `## tests` (exit status plus the last 25 lines of a full `npm test`), `## checks` (exit status of `npx tsc --noEmit` and of the SCOPED eslint run, each with the first 20 lines of output).
NEVER run `npm run lint` or `npx eslint .`. On this tree `eslint .` walks the untracked `.next-old-20261026-130819/` build directory, which `eslint.config.mjs` does not ignore (its only ignore is `demo/**`): it did not finish within a 600 s timeout here, and the round-2 audit measured exit 134 (heap OOM at the default heap), or exit 1 with 7054 errors all from that directory at a 6 GB heap. Repo-wide lint is NOT a gate for this plan; `eslint.config.mjs` and `.next-old-*` are out of scope. Say so in `progress` as a sentence; never put `eslint .` output in the baseline file.
`npm test` currently exits 1 with exactly one pre-existing failure, `lib/web-auth.test.mjs:14` (`isWebPasswordEnabled(undefined)` asserted false, got true). Record it; never fix it.
Steps:
1. From the repo root run:
   { echo '## status'; git status --porcelain=v1; echo; echo '## diffstat'; git diff --stat; echo; echo '## perfile'; for f in $(git diff --name-only); do printf 'added=%s %s\n' "$(git diff --numstat -- "$f" | cut -f1)" "$f"; done; } > .ppm/system-prompt-markdown-panel/baseline.txt
2. Append the suite baseline, keeping the full log outside the repo so nothing new appears in `git status`:
   { echo; echo '## tests'; timeout 1200 npm test > /tmp/ppm-baseline-test.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; tail -25 /tmp/ppm-baseline-test.log; } >> .ppm/system-prompt-markdown-panel/baseline.txt
3. Append the static-check baseline (tsc plus the scoped eslint — NOT `eslint .`):
   { echo; echo '## checks'; npx tsc --noEmit > /tmp/ppm-baseline-tsc.log 2>&1; echo "tsc=$?"; head -20 /tmp/ppm-baseline-tsc.log; npx eslint components/SystemPromptPanel.tsx lib/i18n/messages/en.ts lib/i18n/messages/zh-CN.ts lib/i18n/messages/zh-TW.ts > /tmp/ppm-baseline-eslint.log 2>&1; echo "eslint-scoped=$?"; head -20 /tmp/ppm-baseline-eslint.log; } >> .ppm/system-prompt-markdown-panel/baseline.txt
   Those four paths are the only plan-owned files that already exist; the three files this plan creates are linted for the first time by the tasks that create them.
4. Record in `progress`: the `tests`/`pass`/`fail`/`skipped` counts node reported, the failing test's `file:line`, the tsc exit code, the scoped-eslint exit code, and one sentence stating that repo-wide `npm run lint` was deliberately not run and why.
Verify: `grep -c '^## ' .ppm/system-prompt-markdown-panel/baseline.txt` prints 5; `test -s .ppm/system-prompt-markdown-panel/baseline.txt` exits 0; adding this file changes NO porcelain line, so `diff <(git status --porcelain=v1) <(awk '/^## status$/{f=1;next} /^## diffstat$/{f=0} f' .ppm/system-prompt-markdown-panel/baseline.txt | sed '/^$/d')` prints nothing (the untracked directory line `?? .ppm/system-prompt-markdown-panel/` was already there and collapses the new file); `git diff --stat` is byte-identical to the `## diffstat` section.
Done when: the file holds all five sections with real output, the pre-existing failure is named in `progress`, the repo-wide-lint exclusion is stated in `progress` as out of scope, no tracked file was touched, and no `eslint .` / `npm run lint` / `next build` was run.

tasks.title: Add the pure system-prompt segmenter, stray-tag escaper and their tests
tasks.detail:
Goal: Provide one pure, client-safe module that turns pi's system-prompt string into ordered segments (prose and labelled sections, each prose segment flagged line-oriented or not) and neutralises tag-like tokens the markdown sanitizer would silently drop. Everything the UI does later depends only on this module's exact API. Files: create `lib/system-prompt-markdown.ts` and `lib/system-prompt-markdown.test.mjs`. Touch nothing else: `components/SystemPromptPanel.tsx` belongs to TASK-004; the three `lib/i18n/messages/*.ts` files belong to TASK-002, which runs BESIDE this task, so their ` M` status lines are expected and are not yours. Do not edit `lib/markdown.ts` (652-line hotspot). Never touch `demo/`, `eslint.config.mjs` or `.next-old-*`. Contract: plain TypeScript — no "use client", no React, no Node built-ins — exporting exactly: export type SystemPromptSegment = | { kind: "prose"; depth: number; markdown: string; lineOriented: boolean } | { kind: "section"; depth: number; name: string; label: string; attributes: string }; export function parseSystemPrompt(prompt: string): SystemPromptSegment[]; export function escapeStrayTags(markdown: string): string; DEPTH — one meaning, no other wording anywhere in the file or its comments: a `section` segment carries the depth at which its LABEL renders, i.e. the number of wrapper sections already open when the label is emitted (its parent's depth; a top-level section is 0). The prose segments of that section's body carry `depth + 1`, because one more section is open while they are emitted. PROSE FLUSHED WHILE THE STACK IS EMPTY — the preamble before the first section — carries depth 0, i.e. no indent and no left border. Nothing caps depth. For `` / `` / ``: section depths 0, 1, 2 and the ``/``/`` body is prose at depth 3. RULES: 1. `parseSystemPrompt` splits on `/\r?\n/` and emits a FLAT array in document order. A `section` is emitted when its OPEN tag is seen (never at the close tag), so a parent precedes its children; the body arrives as following `prose` segments. `label` is `name.replace(/_/g, " ")` — never uppercase or title-case here (CSS uppercases; CJK names must survive). `attributes` is the raw attribute text trimmed (`path="/x/AGENTS.md"`), or `""`. 2. Fence tracking runs FIRST, over the whole prompt, before any tag recognition. A fence opens on `/^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,})/`; a later fence line with the same marker character and length >= the opener closes it. Every line inside a fence, fence lines included, goes to the current buffer verbatim and is never structural: a fence opened inside a section body may contain `` without closing the section. 3. STRUCTURAL PREDICATE — evaluated at SCAN TIME, i.e. before `neutralizeFrontmatter` and before `escapeStrayTags` run during the flush (rule 4's order), so no rule depends on another rule's output and nothing depends on escaped text. A line is structural only when BOTH hold: (a) it matches /^ {0,3}<(\/?)([a-z][a-z0-9_-]*)((?:\s[^<>]*?)?)\s*(\/?)>\s*$/ — leading whitespace capped at 3 spaces (4 spaces is a Markdown code block, so the line is ordinary prose), and the name restricted to lower-case `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, pi's own naming rule (this also keeps `` and `Vec`-style tokens out). Group 1 `/` marks a close tag, group 2 the name, group 3 the attribute text, group 4 `/` a self-closing tag; (b) the name is NOT a member of `safeTags` — the sanitizer's own allow-list, built ONCE at module scope as `const safeTags = new Set(defaultSchema.tagNames ?? []);` (import `{ defaultSchema }` from "rehype-sanitize") and shared with `escapeStrayTags` (rule 7). `br`, `div`, `details`, `summary`, `p`, `a`, `img`, `li`, `span`, `input` are members and therefore stay PROSE; `tools`, `rules`, `project_context`, `skills`, `skill`, `name`, `cwd`, `mcp_servers` are not and therefore stay structural. No balanced-tag lookahead, no wrapper allow-list, no second predicate: one `Set.has` per tag-shaped line, testable in isolation. Put in a comment WHY both halves exist: a tag-only line for an HTML tag the pipeline can render (a bare `
`, `
`/``, `
`) is prose in real project docs, and treating it as a section opener both invents a label and — because a close pops only on exact stack-top equality — makes the enclosing section's real close tag fail to match and leak as escaped text while every later section lands one level too deep. Also comment that none of pi's twelve canonical section names is in the allow-list, which test (m) enforces. - open, not self-closing: flush the buffer as prose at the current depth, push the section segment, push the name on the stack; - close: only when the stack is non-empty AND its top equals the name -> flush, then pop. A close tag that does not match the top, or any close tag with an empty stack, is NOT structural: it stays in the buffer as text (the escaper then makes it visible); - self-closing tag line: ordinary prose. 4. Flushing a buffer, in this exact order: drop leading/trailing blank lines; dedent by the smallest leading-whitespace count of the non-blank lines (required — the live skills block indents its XML by 4 spaces, which Markdown would otherwise turn into a code block); trim trailing whitespace per line; skip the segment entirely when only whitespace remains; compute `lineOriented` on that dedented body; run `neutralizeFrontmatter`; run `escapeStrayTags`; join lines with "\n". End of input flushes the remaining buffer at the current depth; an unterminated open tag is not an error (the section was already emitted and its body is the remaining prose). `parseSystemPrompt("")` returns `[]`. 5. `neutralizeFrontmatter(markdown)` (module-private): `markdownRemarkPlugins` begins with `[remarkFrontmatter, ["yaml"]]`, so a body starting with a `---` ... `---` fence would have that whole block DELETED. When the first line is exactly `---` and some later line is exactly `---`, prefix a backslash to those two lines only (first line and the first following `---`). Only the block-start position is touched, so a `---` horizontal rule deeper in an AGENTS.md body is left alone. HTML comments are deliberately NOT neutralised: they stay dropped by the pipeline. 6. `lineOriented` — content shape, never depth. It is `true` iff the dedented body contains NO blank (whitespace-only) line AND every non-blank line matches either `KEYED = /^\s*[\w.$-]+\s*:(\s|$)/` (a `key: value` shape) or `TAGISH = /^\s*\\?<\/?[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*(?=[\s/>]|$)/` (the line opens with a tag-ish/label token). It is computed on the dedented body BEFORE neutralising and escaping, so it never depends on the other rules. A single-line body that matches is trivially true and harmless. Rationale to put in a comment: the 46 KB AGENTS.md body of `project_instructions` sits at prose depth 2, so a depth-based rule put a `
` after every hard-wrapped line of it. 7. `escapeStrayTags(markdown)` returns markdown whose tag-like tokens `rehype-sanitize` would drop are backslash-escaped so they render as visible text. Reuse the module-scope `safeTags` set from rule 3 (do not build a second set). `tagNames` is typed `Array | null | undefined`, so `.includes()` on it is a tsc error (TS18049); the `?? []` is part of the contract. Scan line by line: skip lines inside a fence (same fence rule); reset inline-code state on a blank line; track backtick runs (a run of N opens a code span, the next run of exactly N closes it) and never touch anything inside a code span; at a `<` outside a code span, sticky-match the `y`-flagged literal whose pattern text is /<\/?([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)((?:\s[^<>]*?)?)\s*\/?>/y at that index and, when the name is not in `safeTags` and the preceding character is not a backslash, insert a backslash before the whole token. Autolinks (``, ``) never match, `a < b` never matches, and ``, `
`, ``, ``, `
` pass through untouched. 8. No RegExp lookbehind anywhere (`(?<=`, `(? renderToStaticMarkup(React.createElement(ReactMarkdown, { remarkPlugins: markdownRemarkPlugins, rehypePlugins: markdownRehypePlugins }, md))`. One test each for at least: a. preamble + one section -> prose, then `{kind:"section", name:"tools", depth:0}`, then prose at depth 1 whose markdown is `"- read: Read file contents\n- bash: Execute bash commands"`. ALSO assert the PREAMBLE prose segment is depth 0 (empty stack): with `"Intro line\n\n\n- a\n"` the first segment is prose at depth 0 whose markdown is `"Intro line"` — depth 0 is what keeps it un-indented and borderless in the panel. b. nesting: `` / `` / close / close yields document order project_context (depth 0), prose (1), project_instructions (depth 1, attributes `path="/x/AGENTS.md"`), prose (2). c. underscore names: `` and `` are sections labelled `"project context"` / `"available skills"`, and no segment's markdown contains ``. d. indentation: a two-space ` ` nested in `` / `` is a section at depth 2; a FOUR-space ` ` stays prose. e. dedent: a body whose non-blank lines are all indented 4 spaces comes out at column 0 — assert BOTH `!/^\s/.test(segment.markdown)` AND that the escaped body starts with a backslash-escaped `` token (the string `"\\"` in JS source form). Do NOT expect a bare `"x"`: the escaper rewrites it. f. fence: `` + a triple-backtick fence containing `` + a closing fence + `` yields ONE tools section whose prose body still contains `` inside the fence. g. unclosed open tag: `"\n- a\n- b"` yields a tools section followed by prose `"- a\n- b"`. h. foreign close tag: `"\nbody\n\nmore\n"` keeps `` inside the tools body, escaped (visible) — the body markdown holds a backslash before `` — plus `more`. i. stray close tag with no open: `"text\n\nafter"` is a single prose segment whose markdown holds the escaped ``. j. inline tokens: `escapeStrayTags("Pass --tools, -t , or edit")` escapes the token; `bold`, `
`, `x`, `
` are unchanged; `Vec` becomes `Vec\\` in JS source form. k. immunity: `escapeStrayTags("see and a < b and ``")` is unchanged; a fenced line ` ` is unchanged. l. empty and section-only: `parseSystemPrompt("")` deep-equals `[]`; `parseSystemPrompt("\n/x\n")` is exactly a cwd section (depth 0, label `cwd`, attributes `""`) then prose at depth 1 with markdown `"/x"`. m. canonical order: one fixture containing all standard sections in live order — tools, rules, docs, addendum, project_context, project_instructions, skills, available_skills, skill, skill, cwd, mcp_servers — asserts the section-name sequence equals exactly `["tools","rules","docs","addendum","project_context","project_instructions","skills","available_skills","skill","skill","cwd","mcp_servers"]` and that the last label is `"mcp servers"`. The two `` copies model the real fixture (`demo/mock/system-prompt.ts`): each sits at 2-space indent inside ``, and its ``/``/`` bodies are indented 4 spaces. This test is also the guard that none of the twelve canonical names is in `safeTags`: if one ever is, it stops being a section and this assertion fails. n. `lineOriented` both ways: a `` body of `name: pdf` / `description: Read PDFs` / `location: /x/SKILL.md` is `true`; a two-line hard-wrapped paragraph (`this line is a sentence` / `and this is another line`) is `false`; a body with one blank line between `key: value` lines is `false`; a `cwd` body of `/Users/x` is `false`. o. frontmatter and comments, through the real pipeline: `render(segmentsFor("---\ntitle: Repo rules\n---\n\ntext").markdown)` matches /title: Repo rules/ (metadata preserved as text); the un-neutralised string `render("---\ntitle: Repo rules\n---\n\ntext")` does NOT match /title: Repo rules/ (this is the deletion being mitigated — it must fail loudly if the pipeline changes); and `render("\nhello")` does not contain `hidden` (comments stay dropped, by decision). p. escape integration through the real pipeline: `render(escapeStrayTags("\nx"))` contains `<tools>`, `render(escapeStrayTags("Pass -t , or edit"))` contains `<tools>`, `render(escapeStrayTags("a Vec"))` contains `<T>`, and `render(escapeStrayTags("bold"))` still contains a real `` element. q. PROSE SAFETY — the four cases the round-2 audit probed. Each asserts the segment shape AND the rendered result through the real pipeline: q1. `
` inside a body: `parseSystemPrompt("\nIntro\n
\nMore\n\n\n/x\n")` yields section names exactly `["project_context", "cwd"]` (no `br` section), both at depth 0; the project_context body is prose at depth 1 whose markdown contains `
` verbatim; NO segment's markdown contains a backslash-escaped `` (`assert.ok(!segments.some((s) => "markdown" in s && s.markdown.includes("")))`); the `cwd` body is prose at depth 1 with markdown `"/x"`; and `render()` contains `
` inside a single `

`. q2. `

`/`` stay prose: `parseSystemPrompt("
\nMore\n\nbody text\n
")` is ONE prose segment and contains no `section` segment at all; its markdown contains `
`; `render(...)` contains `
` and `` and no `<details`. q3. `

hi
')` is one prose segment, no section, markdown contains `align="center"`; `render(...)` contains `
hi
`. q4. `` stays prose: `parseSystemPrompt('')` is one prose segment with no `IMG` label and no section segment; `render(...)` contains `` line otherwise becomes a Markdown HTML block that eats the following list and consumes its close tag), a leading `---` fence would be deleted as frontmatter, and HTML tag-only lines are prose rather than sections (rule 3b). 2. Write `lib/system-prompt-markdown.test.mjs` covering (a)-(q). 3. Run the verify commands and fix until green. Verify: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/system-prompt-markdown.test.mjs` passes with 0 failures; `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0; `npx eslint lib/system-prompt-markdown.ts lib/system-prompt-markdown.test.mjs` exits 0 (SCOPED to your two files — never run `npm run lint` or `eslint .`, which is red on this tree because of the untracked `.next-old-*` build directory); `grep -nE '\(\?<[=!]' lib/system-prompt-markdown.ts` prints nothing; `grep -c 'new Set(defaultSchema.tagNames ?? \[\])' lib/system-prompt-markdown.ts` prints 1; scope: `git status --porcelain=v1 -- lib/system-prompt-markdown.ts lib/system-prompt-markdown.test.mjs` prints exactly two lines, `?? lib/system-prompt-markdown.test.mjs` and `?? lib/system-prompt-markdown.ts` (git sorts by path), and you added no other path — the three `lib/i18n/messages/*.ts` lines in `git status` belong to TASK-002 running beside you. tasks.title: Add the four system.* panel keys to all three locales
tasks.detail:
Goal: Land the panel's Copy / Copied / Expand / Collapse strings before the panel exists, so no wave can render a literal `system.copy` on screen. `translate` returns the key itself on a miss, so a missing key is invisible unless the keys are added first.
Files: `lib/i18n/messages/en.ts`, `lib/i18n/messages/zh-CN.ts`, `lib/i18n/messages/zh-TW.ts` — these three are the only files this task may modify. TASK-001 runs beside you and owns `lib/system-prompt-markdown*`; its `??` lines are expected and are not yours. Do not touch `components/`, `lib/markdown.ts`, `eslint.config.mjs` or `.next-old-*`.
Contract: add exactly these keys to all three files, in the order copy, copied, expand, collapse, each with no placeholder braces (so the placeholder-parity assertion stays satisfied):
  en:    "system.copy": "Copy",     "system.copied": "Copied",    "system.expand": "Expand",  "system.collapse": "Collapse"
  zh-CN: "system.copy": "复制",      "system.copied": "已复制",     "system.expand": "展开",     "system.collapse": "收起"
  zh-TW: "system.copy": "複製",      "system.copied": "已複製",     "system.expand": "展開",     "system.collapse": "收合"
Insert them inside the existing `system.*` group, immediately after `"system.label"` (`en.ts:246`, `zh-CN.ts:246`, `zh-TW.ts:246` — re-check the line number before inserting; these files already carry unrelated uncommitted edits, so do not rely on absolute line numbers). Do not touch, reorder or reformat any neighbouring key, and do not run a formatter over these files.
DELIBERATE DUPLICATION: do NOT reuse `i18n.copy` (`en.ts:738`), `i18n.copied` (`en.ts:739`), `i18n.collapse` (`en.ts:1564`) or `i18n.expand` (`en.ts:1565`). That namespace belongs to the settings › translation panel, and borrowing it would couple two unrelated screens. The four `system.*` keys keep this panel's strings greppable next to `system.prompt`/`system.empty`/`system.load`/`system.loading`/`system.label`, the panel is their only consumer, and the parity test keeps the three locales in lockstep. The duplication is recorded as a decision in plan.md §5.3.
Steps:
1. Add the four keys after `"system.label"` in `en.ts`.
2. Add the same four keys with the values above at the equivalent position in `zh-CN.ts` and `zh-TW.ts`.
3. Confirm each new key appears exactly once per file and that no key is duplicated within a file.
Verify: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/i18n/registry.test.mjs` passes; `for f in en zh-CN zh-TW; do grep -c '"system.copy"\|"system.copied"\|"system.expand"\|"system.collapse"' lib/i18n/messages/$f.ts; done` prints 4 for each file; `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0; `npx eslint lib/i18n/messages/en.ts lib/i18n/messages/zh-CN.ts lib/i18n/messages/zh-TW.ts` exits 0 (SCOPED to your three files — never run `npm run lint`/`eslint .`); scope: `git status --porcelain=v1 -- lib/i18n/messages/en.ts lib/i18n/messages/zh-CN.ts lib/i18n/messages/zh-TW.ts` still prints exactly those three ` M` lines (they were already modified in the baseline), and each file's added-line count — `git diff --numstat -- <file> | cut -f1`, NOT `git diff -- <file> | wc -l` — equals its baseline `## perfile` `added=` value + 4 (the same four keys move the numstat column by exactly 4 but the raw diff by 11 when they open a fresh hunk).
Done when: all three locales carry the four keys once, the parity test is green, each locale file's diff is exactly four added lines beyond its pre-existing uncommitted changes, and no other file changed.
